gloss: still; again, more; not any more
title: masih and lagi
pattern: masih + verb or describing word (still) · … lagi (again, more) · tidak … lagi (not any more) · lagi + verb (casual: in the middle of)
explanation: masih goes before something that's still the case: Dia masih tidur (She's still asleep), Masih jauh? (Is it still far?). lagi after a word means again or more: Coba lagi (Try again), satu lagi (one more), sebentar lagi (in a moment). With tidak or sudah tidak in front, lagi at the end means 'not any more': Saya tidak merokok lagi (I don't smoke any more). In casual speech, lagi before a verb is the spoken sedang, 'in the middle of': Aku lagi makan (I'm eating). So its position tells you the meaning: lagi makan is eating right now, makan lagi is eating again.
natural: masih is everywhere in small talk: Masih kuliah? (Still at uni?), Masih di kantor? (Still at work?). Satu lagi, ya and Sebentar lagi are worth having ready from your first day.
stiff: lagi for 'in the middle of' is casual: with an older person or a stranger, say sedang (Bapak sedang sibuk?). And the opposite of masih isn't tidak masih: say sudah tidak (Dia sudah tidak sakit, he's not sick any more).

gap.why: Still open, late in the day: masih. Sudah buka? would ask whether it's open yet.
'Again' goes after the verb: datang lagi. Datang juga would be 'come too'.

examples.registerNotes: A friendly way to leave a stall without buying, or to say you'll be back to finish something.

examples.indonesian: Dia sudah tidak kerja di sini lagi.
examples.english: He doesn't work here any more.

gap.before: Dia sudah tidak kerja di sini
gap.why: tidak … lagi is 'not any more'; tidak … juga would be 'not either'.

examples.registerNotes: Sudah tidak … lagi stresses that things have changed. Tidak … lagi alone means the same.

examples.indonesian: Maaf, aku lagi makan. Nanti aku telepon, ya.
examples.english: Sorry, I'm eating. I'll call you later.

gap.why: Before the verb, lagi is casual for 'in the middle of'; makan lagi would be 'eating again'.

examples.registerNotes: Casual, for friends and family. Politely: Maaf, saya sedang makan. Nanti saya telepon.
